items.summary: `buf format -w` before every commit, no exceptions
items.details: Per rpg-api-protos/CLAUDE.md. CI runs `buf format --diff --exit-code` and fails if formatting drifted. The fix is trivial — run `buf format -w` once — but easy to forget when iterating fast. Pre-push checklist in docs/how-to/run-buf-checks-locally.md.

Per rpg-api-protos/CLAUDE.md. `generated` is force-pushed by CI on every main merge with a fresh tag. Any commits made directly to `generated` are lost. Always work in feature branches from main; let CI manage `generated`.

When claiming `<service>` is unused, grep both rpg-api/internal AND rpg-dnd5e-web/src. The sandbox.api.v1alpha1 package looked unused on first inspection but turned out to be referenced by rpg-api/internal/services/sandboxroom/types.go (an interface stub with no wiring — still effectively unused, but the reference exists). Per Kirk's verify-before-asserting feedback. The unused claim is honest only if `verified by grep on YYYY-MM-DD` is in the doc.

items.summary: `reserved` both number AND name when retiring fields
items.details: PR #136 worked example (encounter.proto:903-905): `reserved 1, 2, 3, 4, 5; reserved "combat_state", "room", "party", "monsters", "doors";`. The number reservation prevents tag reuse (wire safety); the name reservation prevents field-name reuse (TS client safety). Both required. A `reserved <number>` without `reserved "<name>"` allows the name to be reused and breaks TS clients silently.

items.summary: Schema-without-consumer is the seductive failure mode
items.details: The repo accumulated ~5,000 lines of unused proto across 5 services because each was added speculatively ("we'll need this for X"). None earned its keep. Per Rule 4 — no proto unused for >1 release. New services added without a consumer in flight are this trap; delay until the consumer is real. The cost is paid every PR forever.

items.summary: Edit docs in the same PR that invalidates a line
items.details: Per the role prompt and platform-mcp convention. status.md and quality.md are living docs — when a PR adds/removes/changes a service, the corresponding doc lines update in the same PR. Otherwise they rot. Quarterly cleanup PRs are a sign the discipline lapsed.

Per the role prompt. Every claim about a proto detail ("this field is deprecated", "this RPC is unused", "this shape carries dual state") must cite the file and line where it's verifiable. Status and quality docs that say "presumably" or "approximately" are dishonest about what we know. The first reviewer pass on PR #137 corrected several inflated counts (5,650 → 5,577 lines, ~50 → 39 pb. references, ~20 → 27 TODOs). Verify before asserting.

items.summary: Don't force-push a contract change under an in-flight review/merge gate — ping HOLD first
items.details: On TakeAction #170 (PR #171), I reported the contract 'locked + ready to gate', the director ran an independent review gate signing off the 5-value TargetKind shape, and THEN I force-pushed a 6-value shape (NONE restored after toolkit reopened the semantics). My force-push beat the squash-merge so main shipped correct, but the gate had reviewed a shape that wasn't what landed. Director flagged it (logged as wave D15 / retro coordination item). Two-part rule: (1) ROOT — converge the contract COMPLETELY with the counterpart before declaring 'gate-ready'; don't request a gate while any field/enum-value question is genuinely still open. (2) If a contract change DOES land after you've handed off the gate/merge, ping the gatekeeper to HOLD, re-push, and let the gate re-run on the final shape before it bakes to main — never force-push silently under an in-flight gate. The shape is frozen from your side once you ask for the gate.
